name: Boscombe Surf Reef (Bournemouth, UK)
status: DERIVED: every number in "global", "lines" and "extra_layers" is computed by the script from the published 3D-model data (no new measurement); the model inputs and their sources are in "key_inputs" and in the model METHODS_3D.md.

version.name: AS-BUILT 2009 (intact): idealised loft of the verified outline, design crest +0.5 m ACD

frame: x alongshore (true bearing 83.4 deg, toward the east; Boscombe Pier at negative x); y offshore (true bearing 173.4 deg); origin on the 2011-09-28 surf line nearest the reef centroid
datum: z = metres above MSL; model assumes the survey zero is Admiralty Chart Datum (ACD) with MSL = ACD + 1.40 m (Ordnance Datum - 1.40 m at Bournemouth, NTSLF), so z_MSL = z_ACD - 1.40; the alternative reading (survey zero = ODN) shifts survey heights by +1.40 m
shoreline_definition: y = 0 is the surf line visible in the 2011-09-28 Esri image (tide state unknown); it lies about 8 m SEAWARD of the modelled MSL waterline (z = -0.2 m at the line) (model.js shoreline.note). The MSL crossing is computed per line (y_msl_crossing_m).
units: metres; offshore_m = model y (distance from the model shoreline y = 0, positive offshore); elevations in metres above MSL (z up); x = alongshore model axis

method.reef_surface: model.js reef.grid.idealised_z_cm (1 m cells, z_MSL): relief = clip(1 + phi/3.0, 0, crest - seabed), phi = signed distance from the verified outline (m, + inside), crest = design +0.5 m ACD = -0.9 m MSL (flat), outline on the 1 m relief contour (reef.idealised_rule). The viewer re-applies the same cap; with datumShift = 0 (default) the stored grid is what is drawn.
method.seabed: model.js seabed.z_cm (2 m grid, z_MSL): April 2011 DGPS plot colour read (Rendle and Davidson 2012 Fig. 9) in the survey area; thin-plate-spline infill under the reef; CCO beach profiles (2010-04-20) landward; EMODnet-slope extrapolation y > 380 m (seabed_source_code: 0 survey, 1 extrapolated, 2 interpolated under reef, 3 CCO beach, 4 CCO-survey blend, 5 EMODnet slope).

sampling.interpolation: seabed: bilinear on the model grid / analytic profile; reef surface: NaN-aware (normalised) bilinear on the reef grid; profiles at constant model x
sampling.footprint_rule: a reef cell belongs to the footprint if (reef surface - natural seabed) >= 0.10 m (ASSUMPTION, avoids zero-thickness tapers)
sampling.crest_line: x of the shallowest reef-surface cell
sampling.crest_zone: contiguous points on the line within 0.10 m of the line maximum (ASSUMPTION)
sampling.ramp: seaward ramp = from the seaward edge of the crest zone to the seaward end of the reef run (the toe); ramp_length = horizontal distance, ramp_rise = reef-surface drop over it, mean_seaward_slope = rise/length
sampling.max_seaward_slope: maximum over the ramp of (z[y-1 m] - z[y+1 m]) / 2 m (central difference, 2 m baseline), tan, degrees and 1:n
sampling.toe: seaward toe = most offshore point of the reef run (reef surface still >= 0.10 m above the seabed); the reef elevation, seabed elevation and thickness there are reported (thickness > 0.5 m means the model surface is cut at its outline, not at the seabed)
sampling.gap_bridging: gaps up to 12 m along a line are bridged when forming the reef run (ASSUMPTION; only Narrowneck is affected)
sampling.alongshore_length: span = x_max - x_min of footprint cells with reef surface >= level; union = number of x-columns containing such a cell * dx. Two levels are reported because "crest -0.5 m" is ambiguous: (a) z >= -0.5 m MSL and (b) z >= crest - 0.5 m
sampling.offshore_distance: offshore_m is measured from the model shoreline y = 0 (definition in shoreline_definition); offshore_from_msl_line_m uses the first downward crossing of z = 0 (MSL) of the modelled natural seabed on the same line

caveats: The default reef surface is an idealised flat-crest loft (crest level = design value +0.5 m ACD), not a survey: the real Oct 2009 profile tops were +0.05..+0.65 m ACD (model.js provenance).

Slope of the loft flanks (1:3) is an assumption (SLOPE_RUN_PER_RISE = 3.0, source S2); real flanks of the April 2011 DGPS surface have median gradient 0.172 (about 1:5.8) (stats.flank_gradient_median_survey).
Survey datum is assumed to be chart datum (ACD) - not stated in the source; a +1.4 m alternative exists.

centreline.definition: cross-shore line (constant model x) at the alongshore mid-point of the reef footprint bounding box

crest_line.definition: cross-shore line (constant model x) through the shallowest crest cell of the reef surface (ties within 0.02 m: the cell nearest the middle of the shallowest plateau)

second_crest_line.definition: cross-shore line through the shallowest reef cell on the OTHER side of the centreline than the main crest line (for two-arm reefs: the other arm); crest cell z = -0.90 m MSL

reconstruction_check.what: volume of the reef grid read here (sum of max(reef - seabed, 0) over all finite reef cells, no thickness threshold, seabed from this script) against the volume stated by the model for the same version; a check that the surface was reconstructed as the viewer draws it
